statement: The legal-retrieval literature already articulates the exact validity-versus-recency distinction the idea treats as a differentiator: temporal correctness in legal knowledge is described as strictly bitemporal, requiring valid time (when a norm produces legal effect) to be distinguished from transaction time, and 'diachronic blindness' is defined as the failure to reconstruct the state of norms at a point in time, encompassing statutory evolution through amendments.

evidence.quote: from transaction time, when a norm was recorded in the official system
the failure to reconstruct the state of norms at specific points in time, encompassing both statutory evolution through amendments and interpretive evolution through binding decisions
